title: How to Convert Your Hourly Rate to Annual Salary: The Optus CEO Salary in Perspective
description: Learn how to convert your hourly rate to annual salary using the 38-hour week formula. We compare typical pay with the Optus CEO salary and explain tax, super, and casual loading.
salarySummary: To convert an hourly rate to annual salary, multiply by hours per week (usually 38) and then by 52 weeks.

faqs.q: How do I convert my hourly rate to an annual salary?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week (typically 38 for full-time) and then by 52 weeks. For example, $30 per hour × 38 hours × 52 weeks = $59,280 per year. This assumes no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. Use our [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) tool for a quick estimate.

faqs.q: What is the National Minimum Wage in Australia from 1 July 2026?
faqs.a: The National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for a 38-hour week. Casual employees receive a 25% loading, making the casual rate $33.05 per hour. Award rates may be higher. See our [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) page for details.

faqs.q: How is the Optus CEO salary determined and how does it compare to average pay?
faqs.a: The Optus CEO salary is set by the board and is not based on an hourly rate. According to recent reports, Optus key management personnel received $18.9 million in total compensation in the year to March 2025. This is vastly higher than the average full-time adult ordinary time earnings of $2,083.70 per week (ABS May 2026). The Optus Enterprise Agreement sets minimum rates for employees, with annual CPI adjustments.pdf).

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the Hourly to Annual Conversion

When you receive an hourly rate or a salary offer, the first step is to compare them on the same basis. The standard formula used across Australia is:

**Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks**

For a full-time employee working 38 hours per week (the typical full-time week under the Fair Work Act), this gives a straightforward annual figure. For example, if you earn $30 per hour, your annual salary would be $30 × 38 × 52 = $59,280. This calculation assumes you work the same hours every week with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. It also does not include superannuation, which is paid on top.

### Why 38 Hours?

The 38-hour week is the standard ordinary hours for full-time employees under many awards and the National Employment Standards. Some agreements, like the Optus Enterprise Agreement, specify 38 hours per week or 76 hours per fortnight.pdf). If you work a different pattern, adjust the hours accordingly. For part-time or casual workers, the same formula applies using your agreed or average weekly hours.

### The Fortnightly View

Many Australians are paid fortnightly. To find your fortnightly gross pay, multiply your weekly pay by 2. Using the $30 per hour example: weekly pay = $30 × 38 = $1,140; fortnightly = $2,280. This can help you budget and compare with salary offers that are quoted fortnightly.

## Key Pay Points: Minimum Wage, Awards, and Casual Loading

From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. Casual employees receive a 25% loading, making the casual rate $33.05 per hour. This loading compensates for the lack of paid leave entitlements such as annual leave and personal leave. Many awards set higher minimum rates than the National Minimum Wage. You can check your award on our [pay guides](/blog) page.

When using our [the timesheet](/) tool, you enter your base hourly rate. If you are a casual employee, tick the checkbox to add 25% casual loading on top. Do not enter a rate that already includes the loading.

### Superannuation Is Paid on Top

Superannuation is not included in your hourly rate or salary. Your employer must pay the super guarantee, currently 12% of your ordinary earnings, on top of your gross pay. The maximum contribution base for super guarantee purposes is $270,830 per year (2026–27). For a $59,280 salary, super would be $7,113.60 per year (12% of $59,280, assuming the base is within the cap). See our [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) page for more.

## Tax and Medicare Levy on Your Annual Figure

Once you have your annual gross pay, you need to estimate tax. For 2026–27, the resident tax rates are:

- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income over $190,000

In addition, the Medicare levy is generally 2% of your taxable income. The 2025–26 single reduction thresholds are used here because the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed in this estimate. The Medicare levy surcharge (for those without appropriate private hospital cover) and HELP repayments are not included in this estimate.

For a $59,280 annual salary, tax would be approximately $5,092 (using the 2026–27 scale) plus Medicare of $1,185.60, giving total deductions of about $6,277.60. Your take-home pay would be around $53,002.40 per year. Use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) calculator for a more precise estimate.

## The Optus CEO Salary: A Different League

Now let's put the Optus CEO salary in perspective. According to Optus’s annual accounts, compensation for key management personnel rose to $18.9 million in the year to March 31, 2025, up from $15.3 million a year earlier. This is not an hourly rate; it is a total package including salary, bonuses, and long-term incentives. To compare with an hourly rate, you could divide by 52 weeks and then by 38 hours, but that would be misleading because executive roles do not have standard hours. The figure highlights the vast gap between executive pay and the average worker’s pay.

The Guardian reported that companies like Optus and CSL often pay more in executive bonuses than they do in company tax. This raises questions about the link between performance and pay. For most employees, however, pay is determined by awards, enterprise agreements, or individual contracts. The Optus Enterprise Agreement, for example, sets minimum rates for various classifications and provides for annual CPI adjustments.pdf). It also outlines overtime rates (time and a half for the first 3 hours, double time thereafter) and shift loadings.

## Using Our Reference Tables

Our [reference tables](/data) provide the National Minimum Wage, award rates, and average weekly earnings from the Australian Bureau of Statistics. The ABS Average Weekly Earnings for May 2026 show full-time adult ordinary time earnings of $2,083.70 per week. All employees total earnings (including part-time) average $1,579.20 per week. These figures help you see where your pay sits relative to the broader workforce.

## Final Thoughts

Converting your hourly rate to annual salary is a useful exercise for comparing job offers, budgeting, and understanding your tax obligations. Remember that the formula is a starting point. Your actual pay may vary due to overtime, penalties, allowances, or salary sacrifice. Always check your award or enterprise agreement for the correct rates. For the Optus CEO salary, it serves as a reminder of the extremes in executive compensation, but for most of us, the hourly conversion is a practical tool for everyday financial planning.

For more detailed calculations, visit our [about the timesheet](/about) page or use the [job pay](/topics/job-pay) guide to understand how your industry’s award applies.
